newsitem.title: USA: Calif. Assembly OKs tax relief for some companies.
newsitem.headline: Calif. Assembly OKs tax relief for some companies.

text.p: California's Assembly on Thursday unanimously approved a bill to exempt some companies from the state's bank and corporations tax.
The Assembly voted 75-0 in favor of the measure, by Assemblyman Lou Papan, a Democrat. The bill now advances to the state Senate for review.
Companies that are not incorporated in California but store inventory in the state would be exempted from the bank and corporations tax under the measure.
Papan said his bill would encourage companies to do more business in California.
The state Franchise Tax Board estimated that the bill would cost the state's general fund $5 million a year.
